A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable matching despite expansion and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original PC-versus-BP training experiments on synthetic classification, Fashion-MNIST and CIFAR-10, including nonlinear networks and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds CNN experiments on ImageNet-1k and transformer experiments on character-level Tiny Shakespeare.

M1.justification: The core PC updates and linear parameterisations remain. Appendix A.6 adds a heuristic transformer construction with scaled attention/residual blocks and cross-entropy readout, and generalises the Adam hidden-weight scaling to N^(-1/2)L^(alpha-1). The CNN extension was already outlined in v1.

E1.justification: Figure 4 and Appendix A.8 add ImageNet-1k image classification and Tiny Shakespeare character-level language modelling. These substantially extend the represented data and task coverage beyond the retained synthetic, Fashion-MNIST and CIFAR-10 experiments.

E2.justification: BP remains the empirical reference method. Corresponding experiments retain their PC/BP and standard-versus-mean-field parameterisation comparisons, including the renumbered appendix results. The new datasets introduce no additional competing training algorithm.

E3.justification: Figure 4 replaces v1's fixed-width, two-depth experiment using 20 inference iterations and varying activity step sizes with different width-sweep protocols. v2 includes 32-layer residual MLPs using 100,000 inference iterations, plus CNN and transformer experiments using 200 and 800 iterations respectively. Appendix A.8 specifies new cross-entropy, architecture, batch-size and sequence-length settings; these are different experimental conditions.

E4.justification: The activity-step-size sensitivity analysis in v1 Figure 4 is removed. v2 Appendix A.8 adds brief experimental observations about layer normalisation breaking transformer gradient convergence and weight decay accelerating convergence with width. Existing learning-regime, width/depth and parameterisation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions already report three-seed averaging for cosine-similarity heatmaps and qualitative seed consistency where error bars are absent. v2 Figure 1 merely repeats that existing information. The new Figure 4 uses a representative run with qualitative seed consistency, without introducing additional uncertainty estimation or significance testing.

E6.justification: The retained experimental plots are unchanged after matching renumbered figures. However, Figure 4 replaces the earlier step-size results with new gradient-alignment curves for residual MLPs, ImageNet CNNs and Shakespeare transformers. Appendix A.8 also adds layer-normalisation and weight-decay findings. These expand the empirical evidence without establishing same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: The main theorems, corollaries and scaling conclusions remain. Appendix A.6 adds CNN/transformer energy definitions in Eqs. 125-129, while several gradient-transpose errors are corrected in A.4.4/A.5.3. The new transformer specification contains dimensional inconsistencies: Eq. 128 multiplies T-by-N states by weights declared T-by-di.

C1.justification: The parameterisation-equivalence and PC-to-BP convergence claims are retained. v2 adds a transformer-extension contribution and explicitly claims the first demonstration of local BP implementation at scale, elevating this implication in the abstract and discussion beyond v1's more general positioning.

C2.justification: Section 6 substantially expands the interpretation and applicability boundaries. It adds conditional layer-parallel speedup arguments, inference and memory costs, analog-hardware prospects, non-local attention limitations, short training horizons and unvalidated hyperparameter transfer. Appendix A.8 additionally identifies layer normalisation as a convergence failure condition.

D1.justification: v1 promises a future code release; v2 states a specific public code location within the JAX PC library. Appendices A.6 and A.8 add extensive architecture, scaling, inference and training details. New Appendix A.9 identifies an NVIDIA RTX A6000 with 48 GB VRAM for the largest experiments.

R1.justification: Sections 6 and A.2 sharpen the claimed distinction from Ishikawa et al. from an uncertain feature-learning comparison to existence versus necessity of the parameterisation. The discussion also substantially expands connections to biologically plausible learning dynamics, inference acceleration, physical hardware and attention/associative-memory research.

P1.justification: v2 revises the abstract, contribution summary and portions of Sections 5-6, adds a discussion-summary subsection and themed limitations, and introduces architecture and compute-resource appendix headings. The overall section sequence and most background and derivation prose remain, alongside smaller wording and front-matter edits.

P2.justification: Figure 4 changes from two activation-function panels to three architecture panels, and new Figure A.5 supplies a parameterisation Venn diagram. Other experimental plots and both tables retain their content and design, with relocation, caption edits, appendix renumbering and page reflow.

improvement.justification: The new Figure 4 better tests whether the central correspondence extends beyond fully connected MSE models to convolution, attention and cross-entropy. More detailed settings, a stated code location and explicit practical limitations improve empirical grounding and transparency. The gain is tempered by short diagnostic training runs, removal of the inference-step-size analysis and dimensional inconsistencies in the new transformer specification, while the core theoretical guarantees remain unchanged.
